title: streaming(lifecycle): handle client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server-side timeouts
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: streaming connections have historically been brittle on client disconnects, client-initiated cancels, and transient network breaks; customers report partial outputs and orphaned server work resulting in wasted GPU time and confusing client behavior. This PR introduces an explicit streaming lifecycle state machine, robust handling for client-side cancel requests, deterministic server timeouts and cancellation propagation, and a reconnect/resume token mechanism for short-lived network interruptions. Key changes: 1) new streaming_state machine (OPEN, CANCELLING, CANCELLED, DISCONNECTED, RESUMED, CLOSED) implemented in runtime/stream_manager; 2) client cancel semantics: /v1/streams now accepts a Cancel event which transitions the request to CANCELLING, triggers graceful model run stop, flushes prefix cache where safe, and returns final partial tokens with a canonical CancelDelta event; 3) disconnect handling: on TCP/WebSocket disconnect server marks stream DISCONNECTED, retains execution context for configurable grace_period (default 30s) to allow resume; after grace_period server transitions to CANCELLED and triggers resource reclaim; 4) reconnect & resume: issuing clients may attach resume_token returned on initial response which allows the server to re-associate an open execution within grace_period; security: resume_token scoped to request-id and short-lived (default 1 minute) and audit-logged; 5) server-side timeouts: explicit idle and max_run timeouts with clear error events (IdleTimeout, MaxRunTimeout) that surface to API compatibility layer as OpenAI-style event codes for users relying on that behavior; 6) OpenAI compatibility: streaming event framing preserved (data: [chunks]/[DONE]) and we add compatibility mapping for new lifecycle events so existing clients see predictable sentinel events; 7) tests & canary: unit and integration tests for lifecycle transitions, e2e against SDK simulators, and a perf canary to validate no regression in p99 latency under bursty reconnect patterns. Implementation notes: state machine implemented in runtime/stream_manager.{rs,go} (language-appropriate bindings) with lock-free signaling where possible; cancellation uses existing token-cancel propagation into model runner and a cooperative stop path for CUDA kernels to avoid hard-terminating kernels mid-step; resume flow rehydrates KV-cache pointer and continues from last acknowledged token where model supports incremental decoding; for incompatible models we fallback to transparent restart with clear Restarted event. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged for clients that do not use resume_token; new events are opt-in but mapped to OpenAI-compatible frames to avoid breaking naive stream parsers. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind feature flag streaming.lifecycle.controls; canary on dedicated pool then global rollout over 48h with metrics monitoring (orphaned_runs, gpu_waste, stream_resume_success). Migration notes: SDKs updated to expose resume_token and helpers in this PR branch; older SDKs will still work but cannot resume. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] docs updated - [x] changelog entry - [x] canary run passed (see ci checks).

streaming: implement client cancel and cancel delta event
streaming: retain execution context for disconnect/resume and add resume_token
streaming: map lifecycle events to OpenAI-compatible frames
docs: streaming lifecycle controls and migration guide
ci: add integration e2e for reconnect scenarios
review_comments: Priya Shah: Could we reduce the default resume_token TTL to 30s? Shorter TTL reduces attack surface but hurts flaky mobile clients. Reply Maya Patel: Default set to 60s based on customer telemetry; added server config to override per-deployment.

Evan Liu: Need to ensure KV cache pointer rehydrate is safe across quantized checkpoints. Reply Maya Patel: added fallback to transparent restart when model metadata mismatch is detected; integration tests cover a quantized checkpoint case.

Carlos Mendes: What about long-running streams that never reconnect and hold GPUs for grace_period? Suggest exponential backoff reclaim. Reply Maya Patel: added configurable grace_period with reclaim policy and a follow-up ENG task ENG-11022 to explore exponential reclaim heuristics.
release_notes: Adds robust streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel semantics, disconnect handling with resume tokens, and server-side timeouts. Default behavior is backward compatible; SDKs updated to support resume tokens. Rollout behind feature flag.
